topic: Interactive Strength Grows Revenue Following Acquisitions, Eyes More Deals

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Interactive Strength Grows Revenue Following Acquisitions, Eyes More Deals

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The owner of Wattbike, Ergatta and Clmbr posted record quarterly revenue and expects to close its Stepr acquisition by year-end Interactive Strength Inc., trading on Nasdaq as TRNR, reported record third-quarter revenue of $8 million, up 66% year over year, as the fitness equipment company continues to build its portfolio through acquisitions. The company, which owns Wattbike, Ergatta, Clmbr and Forme, also narrowed its losses significantly during the quarter, bringing it closer to its goal of achieving adjusted profitability by the end of 2026. Revenue rose from $4.8 million in the third quarter of 2025 and increased 21% from the second quarter of 2026. Gross margin improved to 41%, up from 17% a year earlier. Interactive Strength’s adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to approximately $400,000, compared with $2.9 million a year earlier, while its operating loss fell to $3.2 million from $6 million. “Q3 2026 is the second consecutive quarter in which the earnings power of our M&A-driven operating strategy is showing in our reported results,” said CEO Trent Ward.

topic: Workout Anytime Signs 15-Club Deal to Expand Across Southeast States

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Workout Anytime Signs 15-Club Deal to Expand Across Southeast States

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The agreement will nearly triple Workout Anytime's portfolio as the 24/7 fitness chain doubles down on recovery amenities and acquisition-led growth. The agreement will nearly triple a longtime franchisee’s portfolio as the 24/7 fitness chain doubles down on recovery amenities and acquisition-led growth Workout Anytime has signed a 15-club development agreement with Tri South Fitness, an investment group led by longtime franchisee Steven Elliott, as the 24/7 gym chain continues its push to expand across the Southeast. The deal will grow Tri South Fitness’s portfolio from eight to 23 clubs across Alabama, Mississippi and Tennessee, with new locations operating under Workout Anytime 2.0, the brand’s updated model that combines traditional gym offerings with premium recovery amenities . Elliott, a Birmingham-based licensed physical therapist who has been a Workout Anytime franchisee since 2011, said his group plans to pursue both new club development and conversions of existing gyms. The agreement advances Workout Anytime’s strategy of partnering with experienced, well-capitalized multi-unit franchisees to build regional density. “When a tenured franchisee decides to nearly triple his footprint, that tells investors everything they need to know about the strength of this brand and where it’s going,” said Workout Anytime CEO Jerry Pugh.
